clue.text: Pedro shocks her, breaking farm worker's implement

indicators.note: something breaking falls apart, so the letters of the first three words come apart and reform

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Pedro alarms a woman by smashing a farmhand's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked staff carried by a sheep minder is the classic tool of that agricultural job.

clue.text: Punishment when worthiest plans go wrong

indicators.note: plans that go wrong fall into disorder, so these letters end up rearranged

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Even the most deserving people get penalised when their schemes fail.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a very mild reprimand or token penalty, a light form of discipline.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for chop is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe something is to chop it
egg is old military slang for a bomb or mine

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing an egg for a vet, as though in a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Egg was RAF and naval slang for a bomb or mine. Vet here is the verb, to check over, not the animal doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to inspect it carefully, the same as scrutinising or checking it.

indicators.note: a woman who keeps something holds it inside her, so her name wraps the next pieces

parts.note: a woman's name
taken as written
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Spider-Woman, the comic heroine, carries a copy of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spider Woman' reads as the superhero, but the two words split: one is the definition, the other a name. RV, the Revised Version, is a common crossword bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvester, or harvestman, is a long-legged arachnid often loosely called a spider.

indicators.note: formulated means put together in a fresh form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman's son drafts an answer to a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is an answer given back, synonymous with a reply in speech or writing.

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
to stem a flow is to dam it

explanation.surface: A firm scheme for building a dam on the Seychelles.
explanation.walkthrough: Dam is a verb here, to hold back, not a wall across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised, set method of working, a fixed scheme for doing things.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A conundrum concerning buses and trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture riddle in which images and letters stand for words.

clue.text: Plant spectacles on mad king's daughter

indicators.note: spectacles sit on a face, framing it, so the two rings of the glasses go either side of the daughter

parts.note: two lenses look like a pair of Os
Regan is one of King Lear's daughters, and Lear goes mad

explanation.surface: Putting glasses on the face of a crazed monarch's child.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant looks like a verb, to put; it is the noun, a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic herb of the mint family, a plant grown for cooking.

parts.note: a brief is informal British slang for a lawyer
an en is a printer's measure of width
counter means against or opposed

explanation.surface: A solicitor supervises steps taken to oppose something.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'oversees' just puts the lawyer above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief Encounter is the 1945 David Lean romance set in a railway station.

indicators.note: to rebuild is to put the parts back together differently, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An optimistic cheer that a country can reconstruct itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Upbeat looks like cheerful; it is the musical term.
explanation.definitionFit: In music and verse, an anacrusis is the unstressed note or syllable before the first strong beat, the upbeat.

indicators.note: the speculator keeps something by holding it inside

parts.note: a bear is a stock market speculator who expects prices to fall
L is the abbreviation for little

explanation.surface: A slow-witted market gambler holds on to only a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Blear describes eyes or sight that are blurred and unclear, so dim in vision.

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O
something breathing is alive, live

explanation.surface: A duck sits breathing up in the branches.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a batsman's score of zero, hence the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is an evergreen Mediterranean species grown for its fruit and oil.

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, so deliveries suggests overs
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone overdoes the parcels being sent to an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries. The Tate is a group of British art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate is to claim more than is true, the same as to exaggerate.

parts.note: a doctor treats patients
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Research reveals that the physician is from England.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor is a verb here: to treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written work examining a subject, a scholarly study.

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: Mineral deposits come first on dry ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains first' puts the remains before the mineral, though the clue names the mineral first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on or towards the beach or shore rather than out at sea.

clue.text: Chapter quaintly cut in certain religious works

indicators.note: in means the chapter and cut pieces go inside the word for certain

parts.note: sure means certain
C is the abbreviation for chapter
ript is an archaic spelling of ripped, so a quaint word for cut

explanation.surface: A chapter oddly trimmed from some holy texts.
explanation.walkthrough: Quaintly flags an old-fashioned form, here a past tense of rip.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture is the sacred writing of a faith, such as the Bible, its holy texts.

clue.text: Fish scholar touring Iceland has magnetism

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so the scholar goes round Iceland

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
IS is the international code for Iceland
an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A fish-loving academic on a trip around Iceland is captivating.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish and the scholar join first, then that pair goes round the country code.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is compelling personal charm that draws others, a magnetic quality.

clue.text: Great power of representative in republic

indicators.note: in places the representative inside the word for the republic

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: A great power held by an elected member in a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a dominant state ruling over many territories, a major world power.

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the vegetable below the river, so it comes second

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: Cooking a duck with greens beneath it, beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a diving duck with a chestnut head, a waterfowl species.

clue.text: Sweet girl embraced by youth in charge

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held inside its arms

parts.note: a cub is a young person, a youngster
her refers to a girl
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A lovely girl is hugged by the young man running things.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubic means angelically innocent and endearing, like a cherub, so sweet.

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
arm means power or might, as in the long arm of the law
aid means help

explanation.surface: A clergyman may be able to assist a helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb of possibility; it is the noun, power.
explanation.definitionFit: A barmaid is a woman who serves drinks in a pub, a bar attendant.

clue.text: Have faith in good exam result

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to believe or trust
second meaning: a grade above a pass

explanation.surface: Trust that a student will do well in a test.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means believe; as a noun it is a merit grade, a mark above a pass.

clue.text: Amaze tedious person with river or sea creature

parts.note: to rock someone is to shock or stun them
a bore is a tedious person
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Astonishing a dull companion with talk of a river or marine life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like part of the wordplay but only joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock borer is a marine mollusc, such as the piddock, that drills holes into stone.

clue.text: Anger about gallons of dirty water

indicators.note: about means going round, so the anger wraps the unit

parts.note: bile is bitterness or anger
G is the abbreviation for gallons

explanation.surface: Fury over many gallons of filthy water.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is the foul water that collects in the lowest part of a ship's hull.

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of paper and the start of duster

explanation.surface: Something concealed inside a cleaning cloth made of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden is the definition here, not the signal for concealed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdu, borrowed from French, means out of sight or concealed, lying in wait.

parts.note: s. is a reference-book abbreviation for see
a giant is very tall

explanation.surface: Look at an enormous hedgerow.
explanation.walkthrough: Hedge is the verb, to dodge or play for time, not the row of bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to evade or delay by being deliberately vague, which is to hedge.

clue.text: Adversary turning up in far-flung surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the remote word goes all round the flipped piece

parts.note: far-flung means distant

indicators.note: turning means the short word that follows is flipped round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An enemy appears in some remote location.
explanation.definitionFit: A disputant is one who argues against another, an opponent in debate.

clue.text: Vance led art and design for item posted early for Christmas

indicators.note: a design is a new arrangement, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Vance oversaw the artwork and layout for a festive card sent in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posted' means put up on a wall, not mailed.
explanation.definitionFit: This card with little doors, opened daily through December, is hung up weeks before the festival.
